target.title: fix(media): guard ffprobe JSON parse against malformed output
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes an issue where `parseFfprobeVideoDimensions` — an exported public function in the plugin SDK — would throw an unhandled `SyntaxError` when ffprobe produces malformed or truncated JSON output. The function is called by external plugins through `openclaw/plugin-sdk`, and callers may not expect a JSON parse crash from a parsing helper.

## Why This Change Was Made
Added a try-catch around `JSON.parse` inside `parseFfprobeVideoDimensions` so malformed stdout returns `undefined` instead of throwing. This matches the function's existing contract (it already returns `undefined` for missing/invalid dimensions) and keeps the fix at the earliest chokepoint — the parser itself — rather than pushing error handling to every caller.

## User Impact
Malformed ffprobe output no longer crashes callers with an unhandled `SyntaxError`. The function now gracefully returns `undefined`, consistent with how it handles other invalid input (zero dimensions, non-integer values, missing streams).

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** `parseFfprobeVideoDimensions` must return `undefined` for malformed JSON instead of throwing `SyntaxError`.

**Real environment tested:** Linux 4.19, Node 22, `node --import tsx proof.mts` importing the real production export from `src/media/video-dimensions.js` (no vitest, no mock).

**Evidence after fix (terminal output):**
```
[case 1] parseFfprobeVideoDimensions: valid ffprobe JSON
  ok: returns width=720, height=1280
[case 2] parseFfprobeVideoDimensions: malformed JSON
  ok: truncated '{' returns undefined
  ok: empty string returns undefined
  ok: garbage text returns undefined
  ok: unclosed object returns undefined
[case 3] parseFfprobeVideoDimensions: valid JSON, invalid dimensions
  ok: zero width returns undefined
  ok: non-integer width returns undefined
  ok: empty streams returns undefined
  ok: missing streams key returns undefined
[case 4] parseFfprobeVideoDimensions: large valid JSON (5 MiB)
  ok: handles 5 MiB payload (first stream extracted)

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 10 passed, 0 failed
```

**Negative control — pre-fix behavior reproduced (same script, same environment):**
```
[case 2] parseFfprobeVideoDimensions: malformed JSON
  FAIL: truncated '{' returns undefined
  FAIL: empty string returns undefined — Unexpected end of JSON input
  FAIL: garbage text returns undefined — Unexpected token 'o', "not json" is not valid JSON
  FAIL: unclosed object returns undefined — Unexpected end of JSON input

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 6 passed, 4 failed
```
4 malformed JSON cases consistently throw `SyntaxError` on current main. The fix makes all 4 return `undefined` and all 10 assertions pass.

**What was not tested:** Live ffprobe invocation (requires ffprobe binary). The proof covers the parse function boundary with 4 categories: valid JSON, 4 malformed variants, 4 invalid-dimension variants, and a 5 MiB large payload.

## Evidence
- `pnpm test src/media/video-dimensions.test.ts` — 5 passed, 0 failed
- Standalone proof: `node --import tsx proof.mts` — 10 passed, 0 failed (4 malformed JSON, 4 invalid dimensions, 1 valid, 1 5 MiB)
- Negative control (main): 6 passed, 4 failed (all malformed JSON crash with SyntaxError)
- No competing open PRs

target.title: fix #99601: fix(opencode-go): expose DeepSeek V4 max thinking levels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 models did not expose `/think xhigh` or `/think max` because their runtime and manifest model rows lacked `thinkingLevelMap` metadata.
- Solution: Add the missing DeepSeek V4 thinking-level map to the two OpenCode Go catalog rows while keeping the existing shared DeepSeek V4 stream wrapper unchanged.
- What changed: Updated `extensions/opencode-go/provider-catalog.ts`, `extensions/opencode-go/openclaw.plugin.json`, and focused opencode-go regression coverage in `extensions/opencode-go/index.test.ts`.
- What was not changed: No auth, endpoint, dependency, transport, live discovery, or stream-wrapper code changed.
- Fixes #99601

## What Problem This Solves

OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 models support the max reasoning effort path, and OpenClaw's shared DeepSeek V4 wrapper already sends provider `reasoning_effort: "max"` when the selected thinking level is `xhigh` or `max`. The provider metadata was missing the explicit `thinkingLevelMap` entries required for OpenClaw to advertise and preserve those two levels for `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro` and `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash`.

## User Impact

Users selecting `/think xhigh` or `/think max` for the two OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 models can now keep that selected level through OpenClaw model capability resolution. Before this patch, OpenClaw filtered those levels out locally before the request reached the provider wrapper, so the selection was effectively limited to the largest lower exposed level.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent root cause for #99601. Related open PRs are handled in the competition analysis below rather than treated as a merged follow-up anchor.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #99637 is an open draft for #99601. #99618 covers the same root area through a broader stream-wrapper rewrite against a related issue.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** #99637 is still draft and did not include the maintainer-ready proof/body required by this flow at the time this PR was prepared. #99618 was reviewed as needing proof and compatibility fixes because it changed existing `high` behavior and duplicated the shared DeepSeek V4 wrapper.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** This patch keeps the production fix metadata-only, leaves `extensions/opencode-go/stream.ts` unchanged, preserves the existing `high -> high` and `xhigh|max -> max` shared-wrapper contract, and adds direct opencode-go coverage for the catalog and wrapper boundaries.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** The proof runs the production opencode-go plugin registration path at this PR's HEAD, resolves both affected models, verifies `clampThinkingLevel()` preserves `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`, and checks that runtime catalog, static discovery, and manifest metadata all expose the same map. It does not rely on mock responses or fixture model rows.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 runtime model resolution now exposes `xhigh` and `max` thinking levels instead of letting OpenClaw clamp those selections away before request construction.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw worktree at HEAD `d13f33be6f1a9ac0e02b2d079479762b0d44ab7f`, using the production opencode-go plugin entrypoint, production plugin-test registration runtime, production `clampThinkingLevel`, production static provider discovery, and the bundled plugin manifest.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
pnpm -C "$TASK_WORKTREE" exec tsx -e '<register the production opencode-go plugin, resolve deepseek-v4-pro/deepseek-v4-flash, run clampThinkingLevel for high/xhigh/max, inspect static provider discovery, and inspect openclaw.plugin.json>'
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
Evidence file: /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-issue-99601-evidence/opencode-go-runtime-proof.log

HEAD=d13f33be6f1a9ac0e02b2d079479762b0d44ab7f

runtime deepseek-v4-pro clamp(xhigh)=xhigh
runtime deepseek-v4-pro clamp(max)=max
runtime opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash reasoning=true api=openai-completions

```

- **Observed result after fix:** Both affected OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 models resolve through the production plugin runtime with `xhigh` and `max` present in `thinkingLevelMap`, and `clampThinkingLevel()` preserves `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`. Static discovery and manifest metadata carry the same map.
- **What was not tested:** I did not run an authenticated OpenCode Go generation request or force a live provider completion, because this bug is in OpenClaw's local model metadata and thinking-level capability resolution before any authenticated provider request is made. The regression tests cover wrapper payload behavior separately, but this real behavior proof does not rely on those tests or on mock evidence.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** The affected users can now select the provider's max reasoning effort for OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 without OpenClaw silently dropping the requested level before request construction.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Review findings addressed

N/A — this is a new PR, not an existing PR repair round. The related #99618 review findings were avoided by keeping the shared DeepSeek V4 wrapper as the single source of truth and by preserving `high` below `max`.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `extensions/opencode-go/index.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** Runtime model catalog rows, manifest rows, static discovery rows, `clampThinkingLevel()` for `high`/`xhigh`/`max`, DeepSeek V4 wrapper mapping for `high`/`xhigh`/`max`, and unrelated OpenCode Go model isolation.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The bug lives at the opencode-go provider metadata boundary, and this file already owns opencode-go plugin registration, discovery, manifest, and wrapper behavior tests.

```bash
pnpm -C "$TASK_WORKTREE" exec vitest run extensions/opencode-go/index.test.ts
```

```text

Tests  16 passed (16)
```

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility.
- **Risk explanation:** The change affects provider capability metadata for two existing OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 models. It intentionally does not change auth, base URLs, request dispatch, live discovery networking, or stream-wrapper code.
- **Why acceptable:** The diff is limited to two catalog rows plus matching manifest metadata. Existing lower-level behavior is preserved: `high` remains `high`, while only `xhigh` and `max` use the existing max-effort wrapper path. Focused tests verify both affected models and an unrelated OpenCode Go model.

## What was not changed

- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: unchanged.
- Channel/provider/session/security behavior outside the fixed path: unchanged; only the two OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 model metadata rows were updated.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, lockfiles: none.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** OpenClaw's thinking-level utility only advertises `xhigh` and `max` when the selected model has explicit `thinkingLevelMap` entries for those levels; the OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 model rows did not include them.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** Adding the map at the provider model metadata source lets the existing model capability and clamp logic preserve the requested level before downstream transport/wrapper code runs.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High.
- **Patch quality notes:** The production patch is metadata-only and keeps the existing shared DeepSeek V4 wrapper as the single source of truth.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `extensions/opencode-go/provider-catalog.ts` owns runtime OpenCode Go model metadata, and `extensions/opencode-go/openclaw.plugin.json` owns the bundled manifest projection. This changes the provider metadata source before downstream capability projection, session validation, and request wrapper behavior.

target.title: fix: use fallback for structured invalid request errors
target.body:
Closes #99174

AI-assisted: yes (Codex).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users routing through Anthropic-compatible providers could see a structured `invalid_request_error` payload treated as an unclassified embedded-runner failure, so model fallback would retry the same failing model instead of trying the configured fallback model when the provider rejected a request format.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing fallback classifier already treats known request-format failures as `format` fallback candidates, but the embedded-runner payload path only allowed a narrower set of provider error reasons through. This change recognizes structured provider `invalid_request` payloads after more specific auth/context/billing/rate-limit checks, then allows that `format` reason to propagate from embedded run error payloads.

## User Impact

Users with a fallback model configured should get the fallback attempt for structured provider request-format rejections instead of losing the turn after a same-model retry.

## What Problem This Solves

This PR restores `google-antigravity` as a bundled Google provider while keeping the Google auth replacement boundary provider-owned, typed, and fail-closed.

The PR separates the three Google paths:

- `google-gemini-cli` imports the official Gemini CLI cache.
- `google` remains the Gemini API-key provider.

This PR keeps Antigravity in scope, but it does not claim a live non-GUI Antigravity model backend. The current Antigravity implementation registers and gates the provider setup surface, documents the runtime boundary, and proves that OpenClaw does not silently wire an unproven runtime path.

The adjacent Gemini CLI path is hardened because it shares the Google auth replacement boundary. Official Gemini CLI cache import now requires validated active Google account identity before auth material is saved, refreshed, forwarded, or staged.

Compatibility note: existing `google-gemini-cli` OAuth profiles that do not carry validated account identity now hit the fail-closed path. Before merge, this needs either a migration or compatibility path for legacy profiles, or explicit maintainer approval for the fail-closed break.

target.title: fix: cap Codex native tool output before replay

Closes #99465
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where oversized native Codex tool output could remain large enough in OpenClaw's Codex app-server projection surfaces to dominate replay-bound worker context even though visible transcript rendering had a separate truncation path.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one shared projector-side cap for native Codex tool output and routes snapshot command output, streamed command-output fallback text, dynamic/MCP projected output text, trajectory `tool.result` output, transcript tool-result messages, and emitted tool-result progress text through it. The cap is `10_000` characters including the truncation notice, and the notice includes the original character count plus the displayed cap.

The change does not claim to fix every future token runaway. It hardens the app-server projection boundary that was still allowing large output text to stay live after a small worker task produced repeated verbose tool results.

The shared script evidence writer bounds logs and failure details, but secret-bearing diagnostics or producer-known private values can be persisted unless redaction occurs before output is discarded. The focused contract tests cover credentials, access tokens, Matrix session keys, recovery material, private message content, default and configured patterns split across chunks, oversized raw logs, and conflicting native artifact status content.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw Talk already has a realtime provider contract and gateway-relay path, but the bundled xAI plugin did not expose Grok Voice Agent as a native realtime voice provider.

Without this, users who want xAI/Grok voice in OpenClaw either cannot use it through Talk or have to fall back to a lower-quality STT -> model -> TTS loop. That is especially limiting for long-running assistants where supplier choice and realtime voice cost matter.

Closes #99087.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one canonical bundled xAI realtime voice provider through the existing Talk `gateway-relay` contract instead of creating a separate voice stack.

The provider:

- connects to xAI realtime voice (`grok-voice-latest`) over WebSocket;
- registers through the existing `registerRealtimeVoiceProvider` seam;
- exposes the provider through the xAI plugin manifest;
- maps audio, transcript, tool-call, cancellation, and close events into the existing Talk realtime bridge contract;
- keeps secrets out of docs and evidence.

The follow-up commits also address the ClawSweeper/Codex review findings: interrupted assistant audio is now paired with `response.cancel` plus `conversation.item.truncate`, the relay playback race preserves the assistant item until truncation is possible, and assistant transcript deltas are buffered so delta-only xAI completion still emits a final transcript.

Dependency note: `ws` is intentionally moved into the xAI runtime dependency set because the new provider imports it at runtime. The repository dependency guard correctly requires maintainer/security approval for the exact head SHA or a maintainer-owned regeneration path. This PR does not try to bypass that policy.

## User Impact

Users selecting xAI realtime Talk get native Grok voice replies through the existing OpenClaw Talk relay path rather than a synthetic STT/TTS loop.

Expected behavior:

- Talk can select `provider: "xai"` with `transport: "gateway-relay"`.
- Gateway-relay clients can stream mic audio and receive Grok voice audio.
- Barge-in cancels the active response and truncates only the currently interrupted assistant audio.
- Completed assistant audio and previous-turn assistant items are not truncated on later turns.

This is intentionally scoped to the xAI realtime voice provider and Talk relay integration. It does not weaken gateway auth and does not include secrets or production token values.

target.title: feat: block broad protected-root shell searches
target.body:
Closes #99466
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex/OpenClaw workers could run broad recursive shell searches over high-risk roots such as a home directory, Codex/OpenClaw state, session archives, repo parents, or external workspace roots. On small PR tasks this can turn command output and local session/debug surfaces into oversized live context, making runaway token usage much more likely.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a high-confidence exec guard for `rg`, recursive `grep`, and `find` commands in gateway/sandbox execution. The guard reuses OpenClaw's existing command-payload analysis so shell wrappers and command carriers are inspected, blocks only protected-root search shapes, and returns actionable guidance to narrow the path, prefer indexed/search tools, and cap output.

This first pass does not add a user-configurable bypass. It is intentionally scoped to the riskiest broad search shapes from the worker-runaway retro and keeps narrowed repo/task/evidence-path searches allowed.

## User Impact

Agents get an immediate, actionable exec failure instead of walking large protected roots. Narrow searches inside a repo or task directory continue to work, and the exec tool description now teaches the safer default before the command is attempted.

## Evidence

  - `src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts`: 8 passed

target.title: feat: block broad protected-root shell searches
target.body:
Closes #99466
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex/OpenClaw workers could run broad recursive shell searches over high-risk roots such as a home directory, Codex/OpenClaw state, session archives, repo parents, or external workspace roots. On small PR tasks this can turn command output and local session/debug surfaces into oversized live context, making runaway token usage much more likely.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a high-confidence exec guard for `rg`, recursive `grep`, and `find` commands in gateway/sandbox execution. The guard reuses OpenClaw's existing command-payload analysis so shell wrappers and command carriers are inspected, blocks only protected-root search shapes, and returns actionable guidance to narrow the path, prefer indexed/search tools, and cap output.

This first pass does not add a user-configurable bypass. It is intentionally scoped to the riskiest broad search shapes from the worker-runaway retro and keeps narrowed repo/task/evidence-path searches allowed.

## User Impact

Agents get an immediate, actionable exec failure instead of walking large protected roots. Narrow searches inside a repo or task directory continue to work, and the exec tool description now teaches the safer default before the command is attempted.

target.title: feat(providers): add Runware provider
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
 
OpenClaw's provider list doesn't include Runware, so anyone who wants to run models through it (DeepSeek, GLM, Grok, Gemma, MiniMax, Qwen, plus OpenAI/Anthropic passthroughs) has no supported way to do it.
 
## Why This Change Was Made
 
Adds `extensions/runware` as a bundled provider with a fully dynamic model catalog pulled live from `GET /v1/models` — no per-model table to maintain, same discovery pattern as vllm/sglang/chutes rather than a baked static list.
Two Runware-specific request bugs are patched at the stream layer: a forced/clamped `max_tokens` and a fix for Runware rejecting the standard empty-argument tool schema.
 
## User Impact
`openclaw onboard --auth-choice runware-api-key` and any of Runware's ~34 live models work immediately under `runware/<id>`; new models Runware adds show up with no plugin update.

target.title: fix: CLI agent session resume churns when owner and non-owner alternate in a group
target.body:
Closes #99633
Related: #99595, #99372

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where CLI-backend agents (e.g. Claude CLI) in group chats with more than one human keep abandoning their resumed session and starting a fresh one whenever the sender alternates between the owner and a non-owner. Each fresh start drops conversational continuity and re-pays session warm-up cost, so multi-person group threads feel like the agent has amnesia every other turn.

Follow-up to #99595, which made `extraSystemPromptHash` and `messageToolPolicyHash` session-stable but left one per-turn input in the reuse key.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveCliSessionReuse` invalidates a stored binding when `promptToolNamesHash` changes. That hash was derived from `promptTools`, which was resolved with per-turn, per-sender facts — including `senderIsOwner`. Because owner-only core tools (`cron`, `gateway`, `nodes`) are excluded for non-owner senders, the tool-name list — and therefore the hash — flipped on every owner↔non-owner alternation, invalidating the binding and forcing a new CLI session.

The fix resolves the prompt-side tool list from the session-stable `cliSessionBindingFacts` seam instead of per-turn params (`senderIsOwner`, `currentMessageId`, `currentThreadTs`, `currentInboundAudio`, `inboundEventKind` are nulled for this resolution; the session-stable `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` / `requireExplicitMessageTarget` binding values are used). This makes the prompt tool listing, the prompt report, and `promptToolNamesHash` sender-independent, so the binding survives alternating senders.

Non-goal / boundary: this does **not** change per-sender tool enforcement. Actual tool availability is still scoped per turn by the MCP loopback bearer token, which is minted from the real `senderIsOwner` (`prepare.ts`, `resolveMcpLoopbackBearerToken(..., params.senderIsOwner === true)`). A non-owner turn still cannot call owner-only tools — the model's prompt now lists them, but the runtime denies the call. `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` is untouched.

## User Impact

In multi-human group chats, a CLI-backed agent now keeps one resumed session across turns from different people instead of respawning whenever owner and non-owner alternate. Continuity and latency improve for the common "owner + others chatting with the bot" case. No change to what tools any sender is actually allowed to invoke.

## Evidence

- New fail-confirmed regression test in `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` mirroring the production owner↔non-owner alternation: asserts `promptToolNamesHash` is identical across an owner turn and a non-owner turn (pre-fix, the recorded bad inputs were `senderIsOwner: true` / `currentMessageId: "owner-message"` leaking into the hash).
- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts` reworked to prove the split: owner loopback callers still see `cron`/`gateway`/`nodes`, non-owner loopback callers still have them denied — the enforcement path is unchanged.
- Local validation (macOS): `pnpm tsgo` 0, `pnpm check:test-types` 0, `run-vitest` on `prepare.test.ts` / `tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts` / `cli-runner.reliability.test.ts` / `cli-runner.spawn.test.ts` all 0, `run-oxlint` 0, `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` 0, `git diff --check` 0.
- Live canary: branch build deployed to a private HamVerBot instance (not merged) to confirm `reuse=` stays stable across real alternating owner/non-owner group traffic before landing. Observations to be added below.

Draft until the live canary shows sustained clean reuse.

target.title: test(qa): redact script evidence diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared script evidence writer bounds logs and failure details, but secret-bearing diagnostics or producer-known private values can be persisted unless redaction occurs before output is discarded. Stream chunk boundaries and oversized raw logs can otherwise remove the context required to recognize a credential while retaining its sensitive tail.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follow-up reuses the public logging redaction contract and adds producer-supplied sensitive values to `createQaScriptEvidenceWriter`. It:

- removes exact sensitive values across child-process chunk boundaries;
- reconstructs bounded raw output before applying built-in and configured logging patterns;
- safely omits oversized unredacted logs instead of truncating away redaction context;
- keeps normalized pass/fail/blocked status controlled by the script result rather than native artifact payloads.

The focused contract tests cover credentials, access tokens, Matrix session keys, recovery material, private message content, default and configured patterns split across chunks, oversized raw logs, and conflicting native artifact status content.

## User Impact

There is no product behavior change. QA maintainers get bounded script evidence that does not persist known secret or private diagnostic content, while normalized status semantics remain unchanged.

## Dependencies

- Builds on the shared script evidence writer merged by #99374.

- Problem: `chat.history` only backfilled external CLI transcript history for `claude-cli`, so Codex-backed sessions could look empty
after refresh when the local transcript was missing.
- Why it matters: users could lose visible history in Gateway/Control UI refresh flows even though the Codex CLI transcript still
existed on disk.
- What changed: added Codex CLI transcript parsing + import support, filtered commentary-only Codex history before merge, merged
multiple bound CLI transcripts when backfilling an empty local history, and blocked old CLI backfill after session reset until a new
CLI binding is established.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no changes to live chat send flow, provider execution, or non-CLI session history behavior.

AI-assisted. Testing: targeted tests + `pnpm check` passed.

- Root cause: the CLI session history import path only supported `claude-cli`, and the import selection logic only chose one external
transcript source.
- Missing detection / guardrail: there was no Codex-specific history import coverage in `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts`,
and no guard for reset semantics with preserved CLI bindings.
- Contributing context (if known): Codex transcripts include commentary/final-answer phases and can coexist with other CLI bindings
on the same OpenClaw session.

  - Codex-backed sessions backfill history from the Codex session store when the local transcript is empty.
  - Commentary-only Codex messages do not consume `chat.history` visibility budget before sanitization.
  - Empty local history can merge multiple bound CLI transcript sources.

available.

- Reset sessions no longer repopulate old external CLI history just because preserved CLI bindings still exist.

```text
Before:
[refresh chat] -> [local transcript empty] -> [claude-cli only backfill] -> [codex history missing]

After:
[refresh chat] -> [local transcript empty] -> [merge visible bound CLI transcripts] -> [history restored]
[sessions.reset] -> [preserve CLI binding + suppress old import] -> [fresh empty session stays empty]
```


## Security Impact (required)

- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (No)
- New/changed network calls? (No)

- Runtime/container: local repo checkout
- Model/provider: codex-cli
- Integration/channel (if any): Gateway chat.history
- Relevant config (redacted): session entry with cliSessionBindings["codex-cli"].sessionId

### Steps

1. Create or reuse a session entry whose local transcript is empty, but whose cliSessionBindings points at an existing Codex CLI
   session.
2. Call chat.history for that session.
3. Reset the session and call chat.history again.

### Expected

- Before reset: Codex transcript turns are restored from the external Codex session store.
- After reset: the new session remains empty until new local or newly bound CLI history exists.

### Actual

- Before this fix: Codex-backed refreshes could show empty history because only Claude CLI backfill existed.
- Before this fix: if multiple CLI bindings existed, only one external transcript source was imported.

target.title: fix: Mattermost interaction token forgeable via hardcoded HMAC...
target.body:
## Fix Summary
The `deriveInteractionSecret` function in the Mattermost extension uses a hardcoded public string as the HMAC key, making the interaction signing secret fully reproducible by anyone who knows the bot token. An attacker who obtains the bot token can forge valid `_token` values, craft arbitrary button-click POST requests to the gateway's interaction endpoint, and trigger agent system events (`core.system.enqueueSystemEvent`) as if a legitimate user clicked an approved Mattermost button.

## Issue Linkage
Fixes #64545

## Security Snapshot
- CVSS v3.1: 7.1 (High)
- CVSS v4.0: 7.1 (High)

## Implementation Details
### Files Changed
- `extensions/mattermost/src/config-schema-core.ts` (+1/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/config-schema.test.ts` (+19/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/accounts.test.ts` (+23/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/accounts.ts` (+8/-0)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.test.ts` (+20/-17)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts` (+23/-10)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts` (+2/-3)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts` (+8/-2)
- `extensions/mattermost/src/types.ts` (+2/-0)

### Technical Analysis
1. Obtain the Mattermost bot token (available via the Mattermost admin panel, gateway environment variables, or any configuration leak).
2. Reproduce the derivation: `derivedSecret = HMAC-SHA256("openclaw-mattermost-interactions", botToken)` — this is deterministic and requires no further gateway access.
3. Construct an action context matching an existing interactive post, e.g., `{"action_id": "approve", "post_id": "<target_post_id>", "channel_id": "<target_channel_id>"}`.
4. Compute the forged token: `_token = HMAC-SHA256(derivedSecret, JSON.stringify(sortedContext))`.
5. POST a crafted payload to `http://<gateway-host>:<gatewayPort>/mattermost/interactions/<accountId>` with the forged `_token` field.
6. `verifyInteractionToken` at `interactions.ts:165-175` passes; the handler dispatches `core.system.enqueueSystemEvent` to the agent as if a legitimate user clicked an approved button.

## Validation Evidence
- Command: `pnpm exec oxlint src/ && pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test`
- Status: passed (with pre-existing baseline failures)

## Risk and Compatibility
- non-breaking; no known regression impact

## AI-Assisted Disclosure
- AI-assisted: yes
- Model: github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4.6

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Mattermost interaction tokens should no longer be forgeable from knowledge of the bot token; the branch now uses a generated or configured interaction secret instead of the old deterministic `HMAC-SHA256("openclaw-mattermost-interactions", botToken)` derivation.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on the rebased PR head `e261bcfab6de7ff05d18d2493ea60aedf234498d`, running the real Mattermost interaction module through Node with `tsx`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e 'import { createHmac } from "node:crypto"; import { ensureInteractionSecret, generateInteractionToken, verifyInteractionToken } from "./extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts"; const botToken = "redacted-bot-token-for-proof"; const oldDerivedSecret = createHmac("sha256", "openclaw-mattermost-interactions").update(botToken).digest("hex"); const generatedSecret = ensureInteractionSecret("proof-account"); const configuredSecret = ensureInteractionSecret("configured-account", "configured-proof-secret"); const context = { action_id: "approve", proof: "after-fix" }; const validToken = generateInteractionToken(context, "proof-account"); const oldForgedToken = createHmac("sha256", oldDerivedSecret).update(JSON.stringify(context)).digest("hex"); console.log(JSON.stringify({ generatedSecretLength: generatedSecret.length, generatedSecretIsHex: /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/.test(generatedSecret), generatedSecretMatchesOldBotTokenDerivation: generatedSecret === oldDerivedSecret, configuredSecretPreserved: configuredSecret === "configured-proof-secret", generatedTokenVerifies: verifyInteractionToken(context, validToken, "proof-account"), oldBotTokenDerivedForgeryVerifies: verifyInteractionToken(context, oldForgedToken, "proof-account") }, null, 2));'
```

- Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "generatedSecretLength": 64,
  "generatedSecretIsHex": true,
  "generatedSecretMatchesOldBotTokenDerivation": false,
  "configuredSecretPreserved": true,
  "generatedTokenVerifies": true,
  "oldBotTokenDerivedForgeryVerifies": false
}
```

- Observed result after fix: The generated interaction secret is random-looking 64-character hex and does not equal the old bot-token-derived secret. A token generated with the new per-account secret verifies, while a token forged from the old bot-token-derived secret does not verify.
- What was not tested: Full live Mattermost server button-click delivery was not exercised in this local proof; focused local runtime proof and Mattermost extension tests were run for the changed interaction-secret behavior.

## Summary
Adds a `runtime.usage` namespace to the plugin runtime, exposing `resolveModelCostConfig()` and `estimateUsageCost()` so context engine plugins can calculate model-cost estimates from OpenClaw's configured pricing instead of hardcoded heuristics.

## Motivation
Context engine plugins, such as [ContextClaw](https://github.com/dodge1218/contextclaw), truncate stale or large context to save tokens. Today they can only estimate savings with a fixed heuristic. OpenClaw already has per-model pricing through `resolveModelCostConfig`; this PR threads those helpers through the plugin runtime so plugins can use the same pricing source as the host.

## Changes
- `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-usage.ts` — adds the runtime usage facade.
- `src/plugins/runtime/types-core.ts` — adds the `usage` namespace to `PluginRuntimeCore`.
- `src/plugins/runtime/index.ts` — wires `createRuntimeUsage()` into runtime assembly.
- `src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.ts` — updates the plugin runtime mock.
- `src/plugins/runtime/index.test.ts` — asserts the runtime exposes both usage helpers.
- `docs/plugins/sdk-runtime.md` — documents the plugin SDK usage helpers.
- `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` — regenerates the public SDK API baseline.

## Real Behavior Proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A plugin can access the new `api.runtime.usage` namespace and call both pricing helpers without importing OpenClaw internals.

- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on branch `feat/plugin-cost-api` at `39b243468f`, after rebasing onto upstream `main` and narrowing the PR to the plugin runtime/docs/test surface.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
pnpm exec tsx .artifacts/pr64436-runtime-usage-proof/run-direct-plugin-api-proof.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal output from a minimal external plugin fixture with `openclaw.plugin.json` plus `index.mjs`; its `register(api)` calls `api.runtime.usage.resolveModelCostConfig(...)` and `api.runtime.usage.estimateUsageCost(...)`.

- **What was not tested:** Full OpenClaw app startup and provider billing reconciliation; this proof is scoped to the plugin runtime API surface added by this PR.

target.title: feat(anthropic): add advisor tool support [AI-assisted]
target.body:
## Summary

Adds support for Anthropic's **advisor tool** (beta: `advisor-tool-2026-03-01`), a server-side tool that lets Claude consult a separate model instance during inference. Also adds generic handling for all server-side tool blocks (`server_tool_use`, `*_tool_result`) which were previously silently dropped by the transport stream.

Fixes several latent issues discovered along the way:
- `mapStopReason` no longer crashes on unknown stop reasons (now maps `compaction`/`model_context_window_exceeded` to `length`)
- All display text derived from API responses is now sanitized via `sanitizeTransportPayloadText`
- Advisor model config accepts provider-qualified refs (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #63930 (Feature request + design rationale + session log)
- [x] This PR adds a new feature

## Root Cause / Motivation

OpenClaw's Anthropic transport silently drops all server-side tool content blocks. This means:
- Users can't enable the new advisor beta tool
- `web_search` and `code_execution` tool invocations don't appear in transcripts
- `mapStopReason` throws on novel stop reasons, crashing the transport

This PR adds the missing handling.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

### New: advisor tool support
Enable in `openclaw.json`:
```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "models": {
        "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6": {
          "params": { "advisor": true }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```
Or with a custom advisor model:
```json
{
  "params": {
    "advisor": { "enabled": true, "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6" }
  }
}
```

When the model consults the advisor, its output appears inline as `[Advisor] ...` text in the conversation.

### Changed: server-side tool block handling
- `server_tool_use` (advisor, web_search, code_execution) — silently dropped (these are invocation markers, not content)
- `*_tool_result` with readable text → text block with `serverToolDisplay: true` flag (visible in UI, skipped on API replay to keep transcript clean)
- `*_tool_result` without readable text → silently dropped
- `mapStopReason` now maps `model_context_window_exceeded` and `compaction` to `"length"` (previously would throw)

## Diagram

```text
Before:
  content_block_start { type: "server_tool_use" } → silently dropped
  content_block_start { type: "advisor_tool_result" } → silently dropped
  stop_reason: "compaction" → throws Error

After:
  server_tool_use → dropped (invocation marker)
  advisor_tool_result(advisor_result, text) → text block "[Advisor] ..." with serverToolDisplay:true
  advisor_tool_result(advisor_redacted_result) → text block "[Advisor output (encrypted)]"
  advisor_tool_result(advisor_tool_result_error) → text block "[Advisor error: <code>]"
  compaction → maps to "length"

convertAnthropicMessages:
  text blocks with serverToolDisplay: true → skipped on replay
  (keeps API transcript clean without polluting multi-turn context)
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? **No**
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? **No**
- New/changed network calls? **Yes** — adds `advisor-tool-2026-03-01` beta header when advisor is enabled. Only applies to Anthropic API requests for Claude models.
- Command/tool execution surface changed? **No** — advisor is server-side, runs inside Anthropic's infrastructure, no local execution
- Data access scope changed? **No**

### Security hardening included

- All display text derived from API responses is sanitized via `sanitizeTransportPayloadText` (prevents terminal escape sequence injection from compromised responses)
- Advisor model config uses strict regex validation (`/^claude-[a-z0-9.-]+$/`) — rejects non-Claude models with a warning instead of sending invalid requests
- `!Array.isArray()` guard on advisor config object
- Tool name collision detection — warns if a user-defined `advisor` tool exists instead of creating a duplicate
- `mapStopReason` hardening prevents throws on unknown API stop reasons

## Repro + Verification

### Environment
- OS: macOS (Darwin 24.6.0)
- Runtime: Node 24.8, pnpm 10.32
- Model/provider: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` via Anthropic API
- Config: `params.advisor: true` in `openclaw.json`

### Steps
1. Configure OpenClaw with Anthropic provider and advisor enabled
2. Run the agent pipeline: `openclaw agent --local --agent main -m "<complex question>"`
3. Observe `[Advisor] ...` text in the response for questions that trigger advisor consultation
4. Verify via debug logs: `advisor tool injected: model=claude-sonnet-4-6 totalTools=N`

### Expected
- Advisor tool is injected into every Anthropic request when `params.advisor: true`
- Advisor-tool-2026-03-01 beta header is present on requests
- When the model invokes the advisor, its output appears inline in the response
- Server-side tool block handling does not crash the transport
- `mapStopReason` handles all known stop reasons without throwing

### Actual
Matches expected. Live API validation scripts (`scripts/validate-*.ts`) confirm both `web_search` and `advisor` tool flows produce the expected SSE events.

## Evidence

- [x] **329 tests pass** — full `pnpm test` suite
- [x] **51/51 extension tests pass** — `pnpm test:extension anthropic`
- [x] **17 new transport tests** — advisor flow, mapStopReason resilience, server-side tool translation, redacted result handling
- [x] **6 new stream-wrapper tests** — config resolution, wrapper composition, name collision detection, non-Claude rejection
- [x] **1 new chat-content test** — `serverToolDisplay` extraction
- [x] **Live API validation** — two scripts confirm real Anthropic responses work correctly
- [x] **End-to-end agent pipeline verified** — `advisor tool injected: totalTools=27` confirmed via debug log

## Human Verification (required)

### Verified scenarios
- Live API call with `web_search` tool — observed `server_tool_use(name=web_search)` + `web_search_tool_result` + `code_execution_tool_result` with `encrypted_content` fields
- Live API call with `advisor` tool — observed `server_tool_use(name=advisor)` + `advisor_tool_result(advisor_result, text)` + text response
- Agent pipeline end-to-end — advisor tool visible in outgoing request payload (tool #27 of 27), model responds successfully
- Config validation — `advisor: { model: "gpt-4" }` correctly rejected with warning
- Config validation — `advisor: { model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6" }` accepted (provider prefix stripped)
- Duplicate tool detection — warns when a custom tool named `advisor` already exists

### Edge cases checked
- Unknown `stop_reason` values (e.g. `some_future_reason`) → maps to `"stop"` without throwing
- `compaction` and `model_context_window_exceeded` stop reasons → map to `"length"`
- `advisor_redacted_result` content → displays as `[Advisor output (encrypted)]`

target.title: fix: accept valid MCP tool schemas without strict inputSchema.type check
target.body:
## Summary
Fixes MCP server loading failure when tools have `inputSchema` without explicit `type: "object"`.

Closes #63602

## Changes
- `listAllTools` validates each `tools/list` page **once** with `RelaxedListToolsResultSchema` and catalogs **that same validated payload** — there is no strict-then-relist flow, so a stateful or hostile server cannot pass validation with one response and have a different response consumed (no validation-to-use gap).
- `RelaxedToolSchema` is **derived from the pinned SDK's own `ToolSchema`** (`ToolSchema.extend` / `ToolSchema.shape.inputSchema.extend`) and differs from it at exactly one point: the root `inputSchema.type` is an optional string instead of `z.literal("object")`. Every other field — `outputSchema`, task `execution` metadata, `annotations`, pagination — keeps the exact pinned SDK contract, so malformed metadata still rejects the page.
- After every page parse, the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` is invoked with the validated tools — the same side effect `client.listTools()` runs — so `callTool()` enforces output-schema validation and task-required guards identically to the SDK flow. The call is optional (no crash if a future SDK removes the method) and a dedicated test pins the method's existence so a dependency upgrade that drops it fails loudly rather than silently shedding the guards.
- `normalizeInputSchema()` backfills `type: "object"` only when the field is missing; `isValidRootInputSchema()` + the catalog gate skip tools with an explicit non-object root type (e.g. `"string"`, `"array"`) with a `logWarn`. Server `toolCount` reports accepted tools only.

## Root Cause
The MCP SDK v1.29.0 `ToolSchema` validates `inputSchema.type` as `z.literal("object")`. Some MCP servers (especially older SDKs or custom implementations) omit `type` from `inputSchema`, returning `{ properties: { ... } }`, which trips a Zod validation error: `invalid_value expected "object" in inputSchema.type` and crashes the whole catalog.

## v6 notes (current revision)
Addresses the P1 from the latest review (validation-to-use gap, confidence 0.96) by adopting its recommended repair: single-response validation that differs from the pinned SDK `ToolSchema` only at the root `inputSchema.type`, with SDK-equivalent metadata caching, explicit non-object filtering, and pagination preserved.
- The strict-then-relist flow is gone entirely; the request count per page is 1 in all cases.
- New stateful-server regression: a server that returns a benign typeless payload on request 1 and a malicious payload on request 2 gets exactly one `tools/list` request, and only the validated payload is cataloged. **Mutation-checked**: against the previous strict-then-relist implementation this test fails with the catalog containing the drifted (never-strictly-validated) tool — reproducing the reported attack — and the server log showing two list requests.
- New SDK-seam pin test: `Client.prototype.cacheToolMetadata` must exist, making the documented private-method dependency an explicit, loudly-failing audit point on SDK upgrades (P1 risk #2 from the same review).
- Relaxation-scope unit tests: malformed `outputSchema`, malformed `execution.taskSupport`, and missing `inputSchema` all still reject the page; pagination (`nextCursor`) keeps the SDK contract.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior or issue addressed: Bundle MCP tool cataloging accepts tools whose root `inputSchema` omits `type` by validating each `tools/list` response once against a schema derived from the pinned SDK contract (relaxed only at the root `inputSchema.type`), backfills `type: "object"`, skips explicit non-object roots, keeps servers with unrelated strict failures rejected, never issues a second list request, and preserves the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` side effects for every page.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS from the rebased PR head, Node 25.2.1, pnpm 11.2.2, driving the real bundle MCP runtime (`getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime` → `getCatalog()` → `callTool()`) against four real out-of-process stdio MCP servers, one of them stateful (different payload per request).

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran `pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1` on both files, plus a live four-server e2e script via `pnpm exec tsx`.

Evidence after fix:
```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  42 passed (42)
pnpm tsgo:core / tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint / oxfmt --check: clean

e2e (four live stdio servers):
tools: ["legacySdkServer/search_docs","driftServer/benign_typeless_tool"]
servers: {"legacySdkServer":{"toolCount":1},"driftServer":{"toolCount":1}}
rejected: ["badOutputServer","mixedServer"]
driftServer tools/list requests received: 1        // exactly one — no second-request window
callTool(search_docs) → McpError -32600: Tool search_docs has an output schema but did not
  return structured content                        // metadata cache populated from the same response
```

Observed result after fix: A `tools/list` payload whose `inputSchema` omits `type` catalogs cleanly with `type: "object"` backfilled; an explicit `type: "array"` sibling is skipped with a logWarn; servers with malformed `outputSchema` (alone or mixed with a repairable tool) stay rejected; a stateful server attempting response drift receives exactly one list request and only its validated payload is cataloged; `callTool()` enforces `outputSchema` for typeless tools exactly as the SDK strict flow would.

What was not tested: A live third-party MCP server connected to an actual model-provider tool call was not tested in this environment.

target.title: fix(gateway): use already-aborted signal in stopChannel fallback
target.body:
## Summary

- In `stopChannel`, when no `AbortController` exists for an account (i.e. no running task), the fallback `new AbortController().signal` creates a signal from an anonymous controller that **can never be aborted**
- `stopAccount` implementations may use this signal for cleanup coordination (checking `signal.aborted`, passing to `fetch`, using with `sleepWithAbort`, etc.)
- A never-aborting signal can cause `stopAccount` to hang or timeout during graceful shutdown instead of completing immediately

### Fix

Replace `new AbortController().signal` with `AbortSignal.abort()`, which returns an already-aborted signal. This correctly communicates "this account is being stopped" to the plugin's `stopAccount` implementation.

### Context

On line 485, `abort?.abort()` is called — so if `abort` exists, its signal is already aborted. The fallback only fires when `abort` is undefined (no active task for this account). In both cases the intent is the same: tell `stopAccount` to shut down. `AbortSignal.abort()` makes the fallback consistent with the primary path.

## Test plan

- [x] All 14 tests in `server-channels.test.ts` pass
- [x] One-line change, minimal risk
- [x] `AbortSignal.abort()` is available since Node 15.12.0; project requires Node 22+

Switched tracks to native GTK. @tiagonix's C implementation was the reference, but I wanted to see what the Rust ecosystem gives us here (borrow-checked gateway client, fewer NULL pointer surprises, tokio for async RPC, `cargo test` for unit coverage).

Happy to fold it in, leave it as a community showcase, or archive it — whichever serves the project.

## What's included

**Library crate** (`crates/gateway-client/`, no GTK dependency):
- Async tokio + tungstenite WebSocket client with auto-reconnect

- 24 unit tests

**GTK4 app** (`crates/app/`):
- AdwOverlaySplitView main window with responsive sidebar (collapses < 600sp)

target.title: fix(usage): handle Daylight saving time (DST) hour boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

This fixes a Control UI Usage-page freeze when a long session spans a local Daylight saving time (DST) transition.

Today the hour-slicing code computes a local `:59:59.999` hour end from the current wall-clock time. In a repeated local hour at Daylight saving time (DST) fallback, that can resolve to an earlier instant and stop cursor progress.

This change switches Usage hour slicing and selected-hour filtering to monotonic next-hour-boundary stepping so aggregation always moves forward in the selected timezone.

## Why

This fixes cases where:

- Usage is rendered in local time
- a session spans a Daylight saving time (DST) fallback or spring-forward boundary
- the page builds hour buckets or applies a selected-hour filter

Without this change, the Control UI can wedge the browser main thread while rendering Usage data for long sessions.

## Changes

- replace the ambiguous local end-of-hour calculation with `getNextHourStart()` plus bounded next-hour stepping in `ui/src/ui/views/usage-metrics.ts`
- convert session hour slicing to half-open intervals `[cursor, nextBoundary)` so exact boundaries do not create zero-duration buckets
- route the selected-hour filter in `ui/src/ui/views/usage.ts` through the same DST-safe helper instead of maintaining a duplicate loop
- add focused node-side regression coverage for Daylight saving time (DST) fallback, Daylight saving time (DST) spring-forward, peak-error aggregation, and full Usage render with an hour filter

## Testing

AI-assisted: yes
Built and tested in: Codex App
Model: GPT-5.4
Reasoning effort: Extra High
Testing: focused local test

- `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run --config vitest.node.config.ts src/ui/views/usage-metrics.node.test.ts`

target.title: # PR: Filesystem Access Control (PathGuard)
target.body:
# PR: Filesystem Access Control (PathGuard)

## Summary

This PR introduces a stricter, policy-driven filesystem access layer (**PathGuard**) for OpenClaw agent filesystem tools, including local media (image/pdf) loaders.

It closes key security and consistency gaps by:
- canonicalizing requested paths before evaluation (realpath-aware, ENOENT-safe),
- preventing traversal and symlink/junction escapes,
- enforcing `allowedPaths` / `denyPaths` consistently for classic filesystem tools **and** local media loads,
- preserving **deny-overrides-allow** semantics,
- anchoring workspace-relative policy entries to the workspace root (and re-anchoring after realpath),
- treating `allowedPaths: []` as an explicit **deny-all**,
- supporting absolute glob policy entries (via minimatch) alongside canonical absolute literals,
- returning structured, remediation-focused policy denial tool results (`policy_denied`) when access is blocked,
- and enforcing a monotonic filesystem policy ceiling for spawned subagents (global + agent + subagent defaults + spawn-time tightening), plumbed end-to-end into the spawned run.

**Important scope note:**

R: “This PR secures filesystem tools; it does not sandbox arbitrary shell execution.”

Remote URLs (`http(s)://`) and inline `data:` inputs are not treated as filesystem paths and are outside this layer.

---

## Change Type

- [x] Feature
- [x] Security hardening
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Docs
- [x] Tests

---

## Linked Issues

- Closes #39672
- Related #8719

---

## Problem Statement (What was wrong before)

Before this PR, filesystem tool enforcement had multiple gaps:

1) **Path canonicalization and symlink escape handling were fragmented**
- Traversal protections and “what path are we actually touching?” logic were spread across tools/flows.
- Non-existent paths (ENOENT) were tricky: naive realpath calls fail and can allow later-creation escapes.

2) **Policy matching was inconsistent**
- Absolute vs relative entries could be evaluated in different “path spaces”.
- Glob vs non-glob entries could diverge in behavior, especially when “roots” filtering was used as an approximation.

3) **Media tools could diverge from file tool policy**
- Local file references inside image/pdf flows could reopen outside-workspace reads if not enforced per resolved file.

4) **Sandbox and host flows lacked a unified enforcement story**
- Enforcement needed to be identical regardless of whether the run is sandboxed or host-based.

5) **Spawned subagents did not have a guaranteed filesystem policy ceiling**
- Subagents needed an explicit, monotonic ceiling that could not be loosened at spawn time.

---

## What Changed (Design + Implementation)

### 1) Core PathGuard enforcement (`src/security/path-guard.ts`)

PathGuard implements:

- **Canonical resolution for existing paths** via `fs.realpath`.
- **Nearest-existing-parent resolution** for ENOENT paths (prevents “create later via symlink” bypass).
- **Symlink/junction-aware comparisons** in canonical path space.
- **Deny precedence**: deny rules always override allow rules.
- **Workspace-only boundary**: `workspaceOnly` blocks outside-workspace access.
- **Relative entry anchoring**: workspace-relative policy entries are anchored to the workspace root, and re-anchored after realpath resolution.
- **Empty allowlists**: `allowedPaths: []` is treated as an explicit deny-all.
- **Absolute policy entries**:
  - absolute **literals** are canonicalized before comparison,
  - absolute **globs** are supported (matched against canonical real paths) without attempting to realpath the pattern.
- **Glob detection** via `Minimatch(...).hasMagic()` (brace/extglob supported).

### 2) Filesystem tool integration (read/write/edit/apply_patch-style)

- Tool FS config is resolved through the tool/fs policy configuration and enforced using `checkPathGuardStrict(...)`.
- Wrappers normalize args and run PathGuard checks on resolved paths.
- `apply_patch` is explicitly guarded by parsing patch hunks and enforcing FS policy on each patch target path (not just args.path/file_path).

### 3) Structured `policy_denied` tool result (model guidance)

When PathGuard denies access, tools return a structured tool result (instead of only throwing a raw error) that:
- states the restriction is system-enforced and cannot be bypassed,
- describes what the tool attempted to do,
- provides actionable remediation options,
- and explicitly points to config keys that can be changed to grant access.

This improves model behavior: fewer useless retries, more direct user remediation.

### 4) Media tool integration (image/pdf local paths)

Local media loads are now policy-checked on the resolved file path:
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.ts`

Key invariant:
- enforcement is per resolved path using `checkPathGuardStrict(...)`, not via root-prefix approximations.

### 5) Sandbox behavior

For local media loads in sandbox mode:
- PathGuard runs in sandbox flows too,
- policy root uses `sandbox.root` when sandboxed,
- otherwise `workspaceDir` is used.

### 6) Subagent filesystem policy ceiling (spawn-time tightening + runtime enforcement)

Goal: spawned subagents must never receive broader filesystem access than the configured ceiling.

Policy sources (monotonic tightening):
- Global: `tools.fs`
- Per-agent: `agents.<id>.tools.fs`
- Subagent defaults/ceiling: `tools.subagents.fs`
- Sessions-spawn defaults/ceiling: `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` (applied when the tool call omits `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`)
- Spawn-time tightening: `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`

Merge semantics:
- `workspaceOnly`: OR
- `denyPaths`: UNION
- `allowedPaths`: enforced as a ceiling/tightening model (empty list = deny all)

Persistence + plumbing:
- Effective policy is persisted on the spawned child session (`spawnedToolFsPolicy`) via `sessions.patch`.
- Gateway plumbs it into the child run as ingress field `toolFsPolicy`.
- Gateway session resets (`/new` / `/reset`) preserve `spawnedToolFsPolicy` (no widening after reset).
- Embedded runner passes it into tool construction.
- `createOpenClawCodingTools` accepts an `fsPolicy` override and uses it as the effective policy for that run.
- Nested spawns inherit the parent session’s `spawnedToolFsPolicy` ceiling before applying config/tool-call tightening.

---

## Configuration (for contributors)

### Filesystem policy knobs

- `tools.fs.workspaceOnly: boolean`
- `tools.fs.allowedPaths: string[] | undefined` (empty array means deny-all)
- `tools.fs.denyPaths: string[] | undefined`

Subagent ceiling:
- `tools.subagents.fs.{workspaceOnly, allowedPaths, denyPaths}`

Sessions-spawn defaults + spawn-time tightening:
- `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` (config default ceiling/tightening)
- `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` (tool arg tightening; can only further restrict)

Notes:
- Deny always wins.
- Relative entries are workspace-anchored.
- Policies are evaluated against canonicalized real paths.

---

## Explicit Non-Goals / Out of Scope

- Exec sandboxing is not implemented here.
  R: “This PR secures filesystem tools; it does not sandbox arbitrary shell execution.”
- No shell argument parsing.
- Remote source governance is out-of-scope.

---

## Implementation Notes (for contributors)

### Policy evaluation edge cases covered

- `allowedPaths: []` is treated as an explicit **deny-all** (not “no restriction”).
- Relative literal entries are **re-anchored after realpath**: if a workspace-relative entry canonicalizes outside the workspace (e.g. it points at a symlink to an external dir), it **does not** match outside-workspace targets.
- Absolute glob entries support symlink-alias authoring by **canonicalizing the non-glob prefix** before matching.
  - When rebuilding the rewritten pattern, the implementation **normalizes slash joining** so root-anchored globs stay semantically equivalent (e.g. `"/**/*.pem"` must not become `"//**/*.pem"`).

### Tool behavior on denial (model guidance)

When a filesystem access is blocked by PathGuard, tools return a structured `policy_denied` result (English text + structured fields) so models:
- do not attempt “bypass retries”,
- clearly communicate what was attempted,
- present actionable remediation options,
- and point to config keys (`tools.fs.*`) for operators to change if access is intended.

### Subagent filesystem ceiling (monotonic tightening)

Effective subagent policy is computed as a ceiling and is monotonic (cannot be widened by spawn calls):
- global: `tools.fs`
- agent: `agents.<id>.tools.fs`
- subagent defaults/ceiling: `tools.subagents.fs`
- sessions-spawn defaults: `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`
- spawn-time tightening: `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` / tool arg `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`

Merge intent:
- `workspaceOnly`: OR
- `denyPaths`: UNION
- `allowedPaths`: ceiling/tightening model (empty list = deny all)

The effective ceiling is persisted on the child session (`spawnedToolFsPolicy`) and forwarded into the embedded runner (`toolFsPolicy` → `createOpenClawCodingTools({ fsPolicy })`).

---

## Verification

- CI checks and tests pass (per latest runs).
- Added/maintained coverage ensuring `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` is applied as a default tightening when the tool call omits `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`.
- Verified critical denial scenarios: traversal, symlink/junction escapes, ENOENT parent-walk, deny precedence, empty allowlist deny-all, sandbox media enforcement, apply_patch enforcement, and subagent ceiling propagation.
- Verified monotonic nested spawning: a tightened subagent cannot spawn a child with broader FS access (parent `spawnedToolFsPolicy` is inherited).
- Verified gateway resets (`/new` / `/reset`) preserve the spawned FS ceiling (no widening after reset).

---

## Reviewer / Contributor Notes (Do not regress these invariants)

- Do not replace per-path enforcement with root-prefix approximations for glob policies.
- Keep deny-overrides-allow.
- Keep relative policy entries anchored to workspace (including after realpath).
- Keep sandbox and host local-file enforcement aligned.
- Keep local filesystem policy and remote-source policy separate concepts.
- Keep subagent policy tightening monotonic (no privilege escalation vs ceiling).
- Remember: exec is outside this enforcement layer.

---

## Rollback / Recovery

- Disable restrictions by setting `workspaceOnly: false` and clearing `allowedPaths` / `denyPaths`.
- No data migration required.

target.title: feat(agents): derive fallbacks from configured model catalog

## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw only derives failover candidates from `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`, so operators who keep multiple models in `agents.defaults.models` still have to duplicate that ordered list manually.
- Why it matters: if the configured primary becomes unavailable, the runtime stops at the primary unless the same catalog is copied into `fallbacks`, which is easy to miss and easy to drift.
- What changed: added an explicit opt-in `agents.defaults.model.fallbacksFromModels: true` that derives fallback candidates from `agents.defaults.models` in config order when explicit `fallbacks` are omitted.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this PR does not change existing fallback error classification, auth-profile rotation behavior, or the meaning of explicit `fallbacks` / `fallbacks: []`.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] UI / DX

- Related #47434
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

- Root cause: the fallback resolver only consulted explicit fallback arrays (`fallbacksOverride` or `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`). `agents.defaults.models` remained allowlist/catalog-only, so keeping multiple configured models there did not influence failover.
- Missing detection / guardrail: there was no opt-in config path that said “use my configured model catalog as the fallback pool when I omit explicit fallbacks.”
- Contributing context (if known): operators often keep a single ordered model catalog in `agents.defaults.models`, so the duplication requirement was easy to miss.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient

- Scenario the test should lock in: derive failover candidates from `agents.defaults.models` only when `fallbacksFromModels: true`, keep explicit `fallbacks` precedence, and keep `fallbacks: []` as an intentional disable.

- Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing `runWithModelFallback` unit coverage already covers explicit fallback ordering and allowlist behavior.

- New opt-in config: `agents.defaults.model.fallbacksFromModels: true`

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[primary model fails] -> [check explicit fallbacks only] -> [stop if none configured]

After:
[primary model fails] -> [explicit fallbacks?]
                    -> [if none + fallbacksFromModels=true, derive from models catalog]
                    -> [try next configured model]
```

- Command/tool execution surface changed? (No)
- Data access scope changed? (No)

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / pnpm workspace

- Integration/channel (if any): N/A

3. Trigger a failover-worthy primary error.

### Expected

- The next configured model from `agents.defaults.models` is attempted.

## Summary

Add a comprehensive memory system deep dive guide, addressing #43032.

### Problem

`docs/concepts/memory.md` covers basics (~600 words) but lacks depth on memory best practices, search optimization, lifecycle management, and advanced patterns.

5. **Advanced Patterns** — Entity tracking with stable headings, opinion evolution with timestamps, cross-session recall via `sessionMemory`
6. **Troubleshooting** — No results, keyword-only matches, `memory_get` file restrictions, MEMORY.md bloat, missing transcript search

Added to `docs.json` under Sessions and memory → Memory group, right after `concepts/memory`.

- Problem: the CLI JSONL parser only special-cases Claude `type:"result"` events and otherwise falls back to generic text collection, so OpenAI/Codex-style fallback runs can lose terminal reply semantics.
- Why it matters: in channel-visible fallback paths, commentary/intermediate text can be surfaced instead of the actual final answer even when the JSONL stream already contains `phase:"final_answer"` and `task_complete.last_agent_message`.
- What changed: `parseCliJsonl()` now prefers `task_complete.last_agent_message`, then assistant messages tagged `phase:"final_answer"`, and skips `commentary`-phase generic item text.
