target.title: fix(status): LINE /status intermittent no-response — fallback, timeout, and retry hardening
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes LINE `/status` intermittently returning no response by hardening the dynamic module loaders, adding a safety-net timeout with fallback message, and cleaning up stale status runtime build checks.

### Changes (10 files, +223/-168)

#### Core Status Fixes

| Phase | What | Rationale |
|:------|:-----|:---------|
| **Phase 0+1** | `.catch(() => undefined)` fallbacks on all 4 dynamic runtime loaders | Previously, a transient import failure would propagate uncaught — now each loader returns sensible defaults instead of throwing |
| **Phase 2** | Eliminate 2 fragile dynamic-import wrappers (`status-message.runtime.ts`, `status-queue.runtime.ts`) via precise static imports; fix `??=` cached-rejection on remaining 3 loaders by resetting promise to `null` on reject | Static imports eliminate the dynamic-hop failure point; promise reset removes the permanent-cache poison so transient failures are retried |
| **Phase 2 fix** | Replace `?? {} as any` false-positive in plugin health line with proper early-return guard | Previously a loader failure would show "🔌Plugins: OK" instead of "🔌 Plugins: health unavailable" |
| **Phase 3** | Add 10s `setTimeout` race in `buildStatusReply` returning a user-visible fallback message | Without the timeout, a hanging render produces zero response to the user |
| **ClawSweeper fixes** | Revert `warn` → `logVerbose` in `logLineHttpError` (P1); remove proof scripts (P1, behavior covered by unit tests); remove stale `createLazyPromise`/`createLazyRuntimeModule` imports (P1, caused check-lint + check-prod-types CI failures); remove dead `clearTimeout(timer)` inside setTimeout callback | `warn` is a theme formatter, not a logger; stale imports were rebase artifact; `clearTimeout` was no-op (timer already fired) |

#### Cleanup

| File | Change |
|:-----|:-------|
| `scripts/test-built-status-message-runtime.mjs` + `test/scripts/...test.ts` | Delete stale runtime build checks (superseded by proper unit tests) |
| `package.json` | Remove `test-built-status-message-runtime` script entry |

#### Tests

| Suite | Tests | Coverage |
|:------|:------|:---------|
| `commands-status.test.ts` | 38 | Timeout path (new), throw path, and all existing scenarios (1 pre-existing Windows I/O timeout unrelated to PR) |
| `status-text.test.ts` | 6 | `??=` retry pattern (new, fail → retry → succeed), channel features, plugin health |

### Scope

This PR targets the specific `/status` no-response failure path only. Broader LINE delivery hardening (reply-token management, push-fallback enhancements) is tracked in a separate open issue: openclaw/openclaw#86012.

### Closes

Closes openclaw/openclaw#94626

---

### Types of Changes

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation (non-code change that improves documentation)
- [ ] 🔧 Chore (refactoring, test updates, CI configuration changes)

---

## What Problem This Solves

LINE `/status` command intermittently returned no response when dynamic imports through the `??=` pattern suffered a transient failure — the rejected promise was cached permanently, causing every subsequent `/status` attempt to hang indefinitely. Additionally, the timeout safety net was missing entirely: if any segment of the status rendering stalled, the user received zero response.

---

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:**
- **OS:** Windows 11 24H2
- **Runtime:** Node.js v24.14.1
- **Branch:** `fix/line-94626-status` (rebased onto upstream/main `0ad58848b3`)

### Unit test proof

- `pnpm test "src/auto-reply/reply/commands-status.test.ts"` — 38 tests pass
  - `"returns fallback error message when buildStatusText times out after 10s"` — exercises the timeout race at the integration level
  - `"returns fallback error message when buildStatusText throws"` — exercises the throw fallback
- `pnpm test "src/status/status-text.test.ts"` — 6 tests pass
  - `"falls back on import failure and succeeds when module becomes available"` — exercises the `??=` promise cache reset

### Known CI caveats

- **QA Smoke CI** — failed due to gateway connection timeout (`runtime-inventory-drift-check` scenario). This is an infrastructure-level flake (gateway unreachable within timeout), unrelated to any code change in this PR. 24/25 scenarios passed.
- **1 pre-existing test timeout** — `"uses provider-qualified model overrides for /status usage lookup"` times out on Windows with slow filesystem I/O. Unrelated to PR changes; reproduces on unmodified code.

### What this proof covers vs. what it does not

| Aspect | Covered | Not covered |
|:-------|:--------|:------------|
| Timeout fallback path | ✅ Integration test through `buildStatusReply` with mocked hanging `buildStatusText` | ❌ Not triggered through a real LINE `/status` command with a genuine hanging import |
| `??=` retry pattern | ✅ Unit test proves promise cache is reset on rejection and subsequent retry succeeds | ❌ Not triggered through a real LINE session |
| Normal `/status` rendering | ✅ LINE screenshots in PR history show working `/status` output | — |

### Limitations

The patched timeout/retry fallback was not triggered through a live LINE bot conversation because triggering the genuine failure condition (a transient dynamic import rejection) is environment-dependent and not reproducible on demand. The timeout path is exercised at the integration test level, and the retry path is exercised at the unit test level.

### Maintainer decision required

This PR adds a **10 second timeout** to every `buildStatusReply` caller. A status render that is slow but would eventually succeed will instead return fallback text after 10 seconds. Maintainers should confirm this behavior is acceptable before merging.

---

## Review status

- ✅ Code review: CONDITIONALLY APPROVED (stale imports + dead clearTimeout fixed)
- ✅ Test coverage: PASS (all suites green)
- ⏳ ClawSweeper review: pending re-review after CI fixes
- ✅ Rebased onto upstream/main (`0ad58848b3`) — clean rebase

target.title: feat(google): restore Antigravity and harden Gemini auth boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This PR restores `google-antigravity` as a bundled Google provider while keeping the Google auth replacement boundary provider-owned, typed, and fail-closed.

The PR separates the three Google paths:

- `google-antigravity` is an Antigravity-owned session setup provider.
- `google-gemini-cli` imports the official Gemini CLI cache.
- `google` remains the Gemini API-key provider.

OpenClaw no longer needs to run a deprecated OpenClaw-owned Google browser callback flow for this replacement path.

This PR keeps Antigravity in scope, but it does not claim a live non-GUI Antigravity model backend. The current Antigravity implementation registers and gates the provider setup surface, documents the runtime boundary, and proves that OpenClaw does not silently wire an unproven runtime path.

The adjacent Gemini CLI path is hardened because it shares the Google auth replacement boundary. Official Gemini CLI cache import now requires validated active Google account identity before auth material is saved, refreshed, forwarded, or staged.

Compatibility note: existing `google-gemini-cli` OAuth profiles that do not carry validated account identity now hit the fail-closed path. Before merge, this needs either a migration or compatibility path for legacy profiles, or explicit maintainer approval for the fail-closed break.

## What Changed

- Added bundled `google-antigravity` provider registration.
- Added Antigravity provider aliases and Google provider model/policy wiring.
- Added Antigravity setup text that points users to the signed-in Antigravity app session.
- Kept Antigravity setup provider-owned.
- Avoided starting an OpenClaw-owned Google browser callback flow.
- Avoided registering a `google-antigravity` CLI backend.
- Avoided writing default model config, runtime config, or auth material for Antigravity while no non-GUI runtime bridge is proven.
- Updated live-testing docs so Antigravity is not documented as a proven live gateway runtime until that bridge exists.
- Added official Gemini CLI cache import support for `google-gemini-cli`.
- Changed `google-gemini-cli` setup to import the official Gemini CLI cache instead of launching OpenClaw-owned Google browser auth.
- Required validated active Gemini CLI Google account identity during cache import.
- Failed closed when Gemini CLI account identity is missing or mismatched.
- Failed closed before save, refresh, forwarding, or runtime staging when account identity does not match.
- Preserved isolated Gemini CLI auth-home staging.
- Preserved inherited Google auth env clearing.
- Preserved Gemini API-key staging for `google` API-key profiles.
- Added provider-owned CLI backend auth resolution through `resolveCliBackendAuthCredential`.
- Preserved generic fallback forwarding only when no provider-owned hook exists.
- Made hook decline fail closed instead of falling through to generic forwarding.
- Preserved backend allowlist checks before and after auth resolution.
- Fixed CLI runner cleanup gaps on mid-prepare failures.
- Updated Google provider docs, live-testing docs, Plugin SDK exports/API baseline, and CLI backend plugin docs.

## Evidence

Validated locally through PR head `54eccc8b7e59b5aaaa2d14d675469a0b5445f4f2`.


Result: boundary confirmed. The live harness selected `google-antigravity/gemini-3-flash`, reached auth candidate resolution, and found no runnable `google-antigravity` setup. This PR therefore does not claim live non-GUI Antigravity model execution.

## Owner Acceptance

Security owner acceptance: pending.

Maintainer approval for the fail-closed legacy `google-gemini-cli` profile compatibility break: pending.

## What Was Not Tested

I did not prove live non-GUI Antigravity model execution. The targeted live gateway sweep selected `google-antigravity/gemini-3-flash` and found no runnable `google-antigravity` setup. That confirms the current safe boundary: this PR registers and gates Antigravity setup, but does not claim runtime model execution until a real Antigravity runtime bridge exists.

I did not perform a live Gemini CLI Google account login. The Gemini CLI path is covered by deterministic cache-import, account identity validation, refresh, forwarding, and staging tests.

I did not run a live official Gemini CLI sign-in cache import through OpenClaw. Before merge, this needs redacted terminal proof showing official Gemini CLI sign-in cache import and an OpenClaw run through the changed auth path.

I did not add a migration or compatibility path for existing `google-gemini-cli` OAuth profiles that lack validated account identity. Before merge, this needs either a migration or compatibility path, or explicit maintainer approval for the fail-closed break.

I did not run the full repository test suite. The focused suites cover the changed Google provider registration, Antigravity setup behavior, Gemini CLI account identity validation, CLI auth forwarding boundary, docs, types, SDK surface, and proof behavior.

## Summary

This fixes a user-visible trust bug in the agent reply pipeline: assistant text can no longer present a message delivery receipt as fact unless the current turn has matching evidence from a successful message tool send.

- Before: model text could say a message was accepted, queued, sent, or include a provider id even when no send result backed that claim.
- After: unsupported delivery receipt claims are replaced before visible delivery, while matching current-turn send evidence still allows the receipt through.
- Scope is intentionally message-delivery only. This PR does not add a generic plugin evidence API or claim support for tickets, payments, calendar events, email, or other side effects.
- Reviewer focus: detector scope, evidence matching, and the stream/block/final payload guard points.

[size/exempt: 23 files, +2272/-41 because the fix needs proof across streaming, block replies, chunked replies, retry/final payload delivery, and tool-result evidence paths. This is not a mechanical PR.]

## Linked context

Related review/proof discussion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94693#issuecomment-4746612520

Current base/head used for local validation:

- Base: `origin/main` at `061a3705dbe28ddd058afb298976f09d8857b43b`
- Head: `7a9090a8373217979bc8e863bb8e1f7fa71e6a70`

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: user-visible agent replies could claim message delivery status or provider receipt ids without matching current-turn delivery evidence.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on this branch, using the production `subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession` bridge with real runtime events and no Vitest assertion runner.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `timeout -k5s 120s node --import tsx` with an inline script that imports `./src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.js`, sends actual `tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_end`, and assistant `text_end` events, then asserts unsupported and verified visible replies.
- Evidence after fix:

```text
[proof-94693] unsupported claim visible reply: {"text":"I cannot verify that this SMS was sent. I do not have matching current-turn delivery evidence, so please check the messaging provider history or use the verified send flow before reporting it as sent.","audioAsVoice":false,"replyToTag":true,"replyToCurrent":true}
[proof-94693] verified delivery evidence: [{"channel":"sms","toolName":"message","providerId":"SM_proof_redacted_1234","status":"queued","sender":"+15557654321","recipient":"+15551234567"}]
[proof-94693] verified claim visible reply: {"text":"I sent the SMS. Status: accepted/queued. Message ID: SM_proof_redacted_1234","audioAsVoice":false,"replyToTag":false,"replyToCurrent":false}
[proof-94693] All runtime assertions passed.
```

- Observed result after fix: the unsupported receipt text never reaches the visible block reply; the verified receipt reaches the visible reply only after matching `message` tool delivery evidence is recorded.
- What was not tested: no live production SMS/Twilio send, no real phone delivery, no full `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` run.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: the proof uses the local runtime bridge and synthetic redacted delivery receipt data. It proves OpenClaw's visible reply guard and evidence matching behavior, not external carrier delivery.

```text
timeout -k5s 120s ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 <changed files>
timeout -k5s 120s ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <changed files>
git diff --check
codex review --base origin/main
```

- Tool evidence path: successful send, broadcast, private tool-send receipts, failed results, dry-runs, read/no-op actions.
- Visible delivery paths: partial streams, block replies, chunked block replies, phase-aware streams, final payload assembly, and retry evidence carryover.

target.title: fix(telegram): preserve forum topic routing
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep Telegram thread-not-found fallback for General topic (`message_thread_id=1`), while failing closed for explicit non-General forum topic sends and direct/private topic sends.
- Preserve Telegram topic routing for automatic async/heartbeat follow-ups by reusing stored topic thread IDs for plugin-owned group routes.
- Seed explicit cron announce targets into isolated-session delivery context so completion and heartbeat notices stay on the configured topic instead of falling back to an agent default group.
- Keep the effective diff focused on Telegram topic routing, cron delivery context, outbound target reconstruction, and the temporary current-main memory-core test-contract shim needed for CI.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests only

## Scope

Telegram extension outbound delivery, shared heartbeat target resolution, isolated cron session delivery metadata, and one test-only `memory-core` mock compatibility update for the current subagent runtime contract.

## Linked Issue / PR

- #78755 independently reported missing `message_thread_id` on outbound Telegram forum sends and was closed as duplicate/superseded by the same topic-routing work.
- #78724 covered the final session auto-reply `message_thread_id` pass-through now present on `main`; this PR keeps the broader fail-closed and async-route preservation behavior.
- Adjacent historical thread/topic work reviewed: #43808, #49704, #52824, #52286, #73900, #12293, #30892.

## Root Cause

The Telegram sender retried `400: message thread not found` by removing `message_thread_id` too broadly. That is safe only for General-topic recovery, but unsafe for explicit non-General forum topics and direct/private topic sends because Telegram can then deliver into the wrong root context.

A separate async path could reconstruct heartbeat/completion delivery from incomplete session metadata. Topic-scoped Telegram sessions and explicit cron announce jobs could lose the thread id before later automatic notices were sent.

## Regression Test Plan

- Explicit forum topic text/media/sticker/poll sends reject after the first thread-not-found error and do not retry threadless.
- Topic-qualified recipient strings such as `telegram:group:<id>:topic:<thread>` fail closed.
- Direct/private and resolved username DM sends with explicit thread ids reject after the first thread-not-found error and do not retry threadless.
- Draft stream preview/materialize sends fail closed for non-General forum topics and keep the existing stricter DM-preview behavior.
- Heartbeat target resolution preserves stored thread IDs for plugin-owned group routes when only `deliveryContext` or `origin.chatType` carries the topic context.
- Explicit Telegram cron announce targets persist session delivery context with the resolved chat id and topic thread id.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Telegram topic sends must not silently retry without `message_thread_id` after Telegram reports `message thread not found`; async heartbeat/completion delivery must preserve the intended topic route instead of falling back to a group/default route.
- Real environment tested: Disposable OpenClaw staging gateway on NixOS Linux, PR worktree `/tmp/openclaw-pr76920-merge`, head `f515e5d36ac1166b955838c21489390dbfd9dbe2`, using `@kesslerClawBot` in a real Telegram forum group (`-1003908474243`). The staging gateway was started from this PR head, and the proof script used the PR's built Telegram runtime, `sendMessageTelegram` from `dist/extensions/telegram/runtime-api.js`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: Started the disposable gateway with `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/home/art/.local/state/openclaw-staging/disposable/openclaw.json` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/home/art/.local/state/openclaw-staging/disposable/state`, then ran a redacted proof script from `/tmp/openclaw-pr76920-merge` that exercised: root chat-scoped send to `-1003908474243`, explicit General topic `-1003908474243:topic:1`, invalid explicit non-General topic `-1003908474243:topic:999999`, and valid explicit non-General topic `-1003908474243:topic:16`.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): Copied live output from the staging gateway/proof run. Full PR comment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/76920#issuecomment-4559064171

  Key copied output:

  ```text
  head=f515e5d36ac1166b955838c21489390dbfd9dbe2
  chat=-1003908474243
  generalTopic=1
  [telegram] outbound send ok accountId=default chatId=-1003908474243 messageId=14 operation=sendMessage deliveryKind=text chunkCount=1
  rootSend=ok messageId=14 chatId=-1003908474243
  [telegram] outbound send ok accountId=default chatId=-1003908474243 messageId=15 operation=sendMessage deliveryKind=text chunkCount=1
  generalTopicSend=ok messageId=15 chatId=-1003908474243 topic=1
  [telegram] message failed: Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: message thread not found)
  invalidTopicSend=failed_closed topic=999999
  invalidTopicCheck=no_threadless_retry_observed

  nonGeneralTopicProof=head=f515e5d36ac1166b955838c21489390dbfd9dbe2
  nonGeneralTopic=16
  [telegram] outbound send ok accountId=default chatId=-1003908474243 messageId=17 operation=sendMessage deliveryKind=text threadId=16 chunkCount=1
  nonGeneralTopicSend=ok messageId=17 chatId=-1003908474243 topic=16
  ```
- Observed result after fix: Root chat-scoped send succeeded without a topic/thread id; General topic delivery succeeded and remained chat-scoped; an invalid explicit non-General forum topic failed closed and did not retry threadless; a valid explicit non-General forum topic sent with `threadId=16`, proving delivery stayed in the requested forum topic.
- What was not tested: I did not run a full live cron or heartbeat follow-up through the gateway in this proof pass. Existing focused tests still cover cron session delivery context and heartbeat topic-route reconstruction.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: The live proof covers the real Telegram transport and topic send path. Cron/heartbeat route reconstruction remains covered by focused regression tests rather than a scheduled end-to-end cron/heartbeat run.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): ClawSweeper's current-main/source review for this PR identifies the pre-patch failure mode: explicit Telegram topic sends could retry threadless after `message thread not found`, and async follow-up routing could lose topic context. The after-fix proof above shows the explicit send path no longer retries threadless for an invalid non-General topic.

## Verification

Current head `75acdc52684b07c8355966394f5ad5347a713e0a` was refreshed against latest `origin/main`, trimmed back to the intended nine-file effective diff, and pushed after the commands above passed locally.

## Security Impact

Reduces cross-topic message leakage in Telegram forum groups and private/direct topic contexts by failing closed when an explicit thread is stale or invalid, and by preserving topic context for automatic follow-up notices.

## Compatibility / Migration

No config migration. Non-General forum topic and direct/private topic sends now surface the Telegram error instead of silently retrying threadless. Explicit cron announce routes now persist the intended delivery context for later automatic notices.

## Risks

If an operator intentionally relied on stale explicit topic sends falling back to a root chat, those sends now fail. That behavior was the leakage bug this PR is meant to prevent.

The cron/session change is intentionally limited to resolved explicit delivery targets; bare `delivery.mode: none` jobs still avoid implicit last-target resolution.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted refresh, simplification, validation, and PR-body update.

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

## Evidence

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.test.ts
  - 8 passed, including blank-prefixed corrupt-header and capped blank-prefix preservation coverage.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts
  - 24 passed.
- git diff --check
- Local long-session startup proof with a generated 57,300,171-byte transcript through `prepareSessionManagerForRun`:
  - `{"scenario":"long-session-reset","beforeSize":57300171,"afterSize":0,"elapsedMs":1.22}`
  - `{"scenario":"capped-blank-prefix-corrupt-header","rejected":true,"preserved":true,"elapsedMs":12.07}`

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation


## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78451
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-78451` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14. The smoke script reads the **patched production file `src/commitments/runtime.ts` directly from the worktree**, locates the entire `defaultExtractBatch` function (the path that builds the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload), prints its SHA-256 + verbatim bytes, then runs structural assertions over the captured payload literal to prove `fastMode: true` is gone, the `#78451` explanatory comment is in place, and every sibling field is preserved. No mocks, no test runner — the patched source bytes drive the smoke. PR head: `a3189f329687fa8c2c9da783afbc0d644ea94573`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `git checkout fix/commitments-no-fastmode-hardcode && node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts`, where `smoke-pr78459.mts` reads `src/commitments/runtime.ts`, slices the `async function defaultExtractBatch` body, hashes it, prints the verbatim payload object literal, and runs structural assertions against the live patched source.
- Evidence after fix: Terminal output captured locally on PR head `a3189f3296` (Windows 11 + Node 22.14, the patched `src/commitments/runtime.ts` `defaultExtractBatch` function read from the worktree, 1660 bytes, SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379`).

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): bound suite runtime gateway JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.ts` used an unbounded
`await response.json()` on the gateway HTTP success path inside `fetchJson`.
A misbehaving or hostile gateway endpoint (or accidental huge payload) could
stream oversized JSON and trigger unbounded allocation during `JSON.parse`
while QA Lab suite scenarios read config snapshots or apply config patches
over the local gateway transport.

Replacing the success read with `readProviderJsonResponse` caps JSON parsing at
16 MiB and emits labeled errors such as
`qa-lab-suite-fetch-json: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`.

This aligns QA Lab's suite runtime gateway with the broader OpenClaw
response-limit campaign that already bounded sibling provider and channel
surfaces (Telegram plugin Bot API reads, Copilot token exchange, Google OAuth,
QA Lab Telegram live transport, etc.).

## Changes

* `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.ts`:
  - imports `readProviderJsonResponse` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`
  - replaces `await response.json()` with
    `readProviderJsonResponse(response, "qa-lab-suite-fetch-json")` in
    `fetchJson`

* `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.test.ts`:
  - adds regression test `bounds oversized suite gateway JSON responses` using a
    real `Response` object and asserting the labeled cap error

* `scripts/proof-qa-lab-suite-gateway-bound.mjs`:
  - path-level proof over `node:http` streaming gateway envelopes plus vitest
    regression hook

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Oversized gateway JSON success bodies fail closed
instead of unbounded `JSON.parse` allocation on the QA Lab suite runtime
gateway path.

**Real environment tested:** Node v22.22.0, macOS 15.3.1, `node:http` streaming
server on `127.0.0.1`, built helper from `dist/plugin-sdk/provider-http.js`.

**Exact steps:**
1. Stream an ~18 MiB gateway `{ payload: ... }` envelope from a local HTTP
   server (no `Content-Length`).
2. Drive `readProviderJsonResponse` with label `qa-lab-suite-fetch-json` → assert
   labeled parse cap.
3. Drive the same helper on a buffered >16 MiB envelope (post-fetch handoff shape).
4. Verify a normal config snapshot envelope still parses.
5. Negative control: unbounded `response.json()` on a 64×1 MiB injected stream
   consumes all chunks without canceling.
6. Bounded helper cancels early on the same injected stream.
7. Run qa-lab vitest regression via `fetchJson("http://127.0.0.1:43123/config")`.

**Observed result:**
- Parse boundary (stream): `qa-lab-suite-fetch-json: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`
- Buffered oversized envelope: 16 778 254 bytes rejected before `JSON.parse`
- Normal config snapshot envelope parses with hash intact
- Negative control: unbounded `.json()` read all 64 chunks; bounded helper stopped at
  readCount=17 and invoked `cancel()`
- `ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED`

**What was not tested:** live QA Lab suite runs against a real OpenClaw gateway process.

## Evidence

```
=== QA Lab suite gateway bound proof (path-level) ===
--- Case 1: oversized streamed gateway body rejected at parse boundary ---
  ok: readProviderJsonResponse rejects oversized streamed gateway body
  ok: parse-boundary label present (got: qa-lab-suite-fetch-json: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes)

--- Case 2: oversized buffered gateway envelope (production handoff) ---
  ok: buffered oversized gateway body rejected before JSON.parse
  ok: body size 16778254 bytes exceeds 16777216 cap

--- Case 3: normal gateway config snapshot still parses ---
  ok: config snapshot envelope parses
  ok: config object intact

--- Case 4: negative control — unbounded response.json() ---
  ok: unbounded .json() consumed all 64 chunks (readCount=64)
  ok: stream NOT cancelled via .cancel()

--- Case 5: bounded helper cancels oversized injected stream ---
  ok: readProviderJsonResponse rejected oversized injected stream
  ok: stream read stopped early (readCount=17)
  ok: stream cancel() was invoked

--- Case 6: qa-lab suite gateway regression test ---
  Tests  1 passed | 12 skipped (13)
  ok: vitest qa-lab suite gateway bound regression test passed

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

```
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test \
  extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.test.ts \
  -t "bounds oversized suite gateway JSON responses"
# Tests  1 passed | 12 skipped (13)
```

New bound regression test (1 added):
- `bounds oversized suite gateway JSON responses` ✓

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
